samples.summary: `login` resolves the server itself (`parentOpts.server ?? DEFAULT_SERVER`) and ignores `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER` and the config profile — contradicting the contract this delta re-asserts in the doc comment it rewrote, and inconsistent with every other command
samples.evidence: login.ts:25 does `const server = (parentOpts.server ?? DEFAULT_SERVER).replace(/\/$/, '')`. Every other command goes through `getConfig()` → `resolveConfig()` (packages/cli/src/commands/root.ts:29-36, packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:90-94/115-119/137-141/154-158), which prefers `flags.server ?? process.env.WAFFLEBASE_SERVER ?? session.server ?? profile.server ?? DEFAULT_SERVER`. `--server` has no `.env()` binding on the root program (root.ts:64), so nothing else supplies the env var to `login`. The delta's rewritten docstring (login.ts:219) and the design doc (docs/design/cli.md:226-228) both state the CLI is pointed at a server via "`--server` / `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER`, self-hosting". Concrete blast: a self-hoster who exports `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER=https://wb.internal` and runs `wafflebase login` authenticates against `https://api.wafflebase.io` and saves `session.server` = the default; every subsequent command then uses the env server with tokens minted by a different one, producing 401s. Fix belongs in login.ts (route through `resolveConfig`), not in the new code.

samples.summary: Design doc still states the timeout message unconditionally, while the delta made it conditional on an attacker-triggerable flag
samples.evidence: docs/design/cli.md:191-194 says "shuts down after the callback with a 30-second timeout. On timeout it prints: 'Login timed out. Try again with `wafflebase login`.'" After this delta, login.ts:373-382 emits UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE instead whenever any nonce-less `/callback` was seen. cli.md:233-234 later describes the substitution, so the two paragraphs of the same doc now disagree; the earlier one is the stale copy left behind by the delta.

samples.summary: `close()` calls `srv.close()` only, which does not tear down idle keep-alive sockets; the new `/start` hop adds a second browser socket that can keep the CLI process alive after a successful login
samples.evidence: close() at login.ts:404-407 does `clearTimeout(timeout); srv.close()`. `server.close()` stops accepting but leaves established keep-alive connections (and their handles) open until the peer or `keepAliveTimeout` closes them; there is no `srv.closeAllConnections()`/`closeIdleConnections()` anywhere in the package (grep for `closeAllConnections` returns nothing). Before this delta the browser made one loopback request (`/callback`); it now makes `/start` first, so an extra idle socket can linger. The action handler ends at login.ts:169 with no `process.exit`, so `runCli` returns and the process only exits once every handle is released — a visible hang of up to the keep-alive timeout after "Logged in as X.". Would need confirming against the Node version the CLI targets (newer Node closes idle connections on `close()`).

verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as claimed: login.ts:25 resolves `server` as `(parentOpts.server ?? DEFAULT_SERVER)` with no call to resolveConfig (only DEFAULT_SERVER is imported, login.ts:11). The root `--server` option has no `.env()` binding (root.ts:64), so `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER` never reaches `parentOpts.server`; nothing else supplies it to login. Every other command resolves the server via root.ts:29-36 → config.ts:90-94/115-119/137-141/154-158, which prefers `flags.server ?? process.env.WAFFLEBASE_SERVER ?? session.server ?? profile.server ?? DEFAULT_SERVER`. Env var and profile `server` are documented CLI-wide config (packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:92-98, 76-84) and re-asserted in login.ts:219 and docs/design/cli.md:226-228. Consequence: login authenticates against and persists `session.server` (login.ts:159) as the default while later commands use the env/profile server with tokens minted by a different server. No guard, caller, or test (packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts covers only the callback listener) makes this unreachable, and the defect is a cross-module writer/reader contract mismatch on `session.server`, which is within the blast-radius lane at major.
